nodes.label: Google Drive file scope
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: The narrow drive.file scope is preferred because it limits access to files created, opened, or shared with the app and avoids broader restricted scopes.

nodes.label: Drive resumable upload protocol
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: The protocol provides a session URI, Content-Range progress, and recovery inspection; clients must not assume a lost response means no bytes were accepted.

nodes.label: OAuth state and redirect integrity
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: Random server-side state, exact redirect matching, backend-held secrets, and clean post-callback redirects reduce CSRF, replay, and code exposure risk.

nodes.label: Drive changes cursor
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: A stored start page token and post-processing cursor advance provide efficient, recoverable change detection without replacing the ownership database.

nodes.label: R2 presigned capability model
nodes.author: Cloudflare
nodes.rationale: R2 presigned URLs are bearer tokens, so Storvia must issue them short-lived and operation-scoped rather than treating them as ordinary links.

nodes.label: RFC 9457 error shape
nodes.author: onurcinar
nodes.rationale: A standard application/problem+json body avoids forcing each client to learn a private error envelope.

nodes.label: ServeMux routing benchmark
nodes.author: rosgluk
nodes.rationale: The cited benchmark found the standard library router competitive while reducing dependencies, and the database dominates the request budget anyway.

nodes.label: Research source limitations
nodes.rationale: Provider behavior and community evidence can change or be anecdotal, so real file types, users, account mixes, and regions still require validation.
